llm_proposer.assessment: The outage is most consistent with a hard WSS input-port failure in the ROADM at S20. S20 is the sole stated common dependency of all affected working paths, while the simultaneous hard optical LOS and protection reactions favor a shared optical blocking fault over individual client, transceiver, or OTN faults; the adjacent OSC alarms are not fully explained by a WSS failure and may indicate a broader unmodeled S20 site failure.

proposals.rationale: A failed WSS input port at the common S20 ROADM can simultaneously block all channels using that port, matching the widespread OCH_LOS, client failures, and protection switching at t=602.5 s. The main counterevidence is that a WSS fault should not itself remove OSC on multiple S20-adjacent spans.

A switch-fabric failure at the common site could interrupt many ODUs simultaneously. It is unlikely because it would produce ODU-layer effects rather than the numerous OCH_LOS and OSC_LOS alarms observed.
proposals.note: site named; its node equipment does not document the mode

proposals.rationale: A disconnected OMS input near S20 would cause hard all-channel loss and could account for AMP_INPUT_LOS. A single connector does not readily explain the simultaneous losses on both the S20–S01 and S20–S13 directions.

Severe loss on the span preceding O1 is consistent with both AMP_INPUT_LOS and the OSC loss on the first S20–S01 span. It explains only one branch, whereas the event simultaneously affects several S20-adjacent directions and the whole common service set.
